ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, P is a point on the diagonal AC of the rhombus ABCD, $PE\perp AB$ at point E, and $PF\perp AD$ at point F. Given that $\angle BAD=60^\circ$, $PE=1$, find the length of AE.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus and $\angle BAD=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle PAE=30^\circ$\\
Since $PE \perp AB$,\\
it follows that $AP=2PE=2$,\\
therefore $AE=\sqrt{AP^{2}-PE^{2}}=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a rhombus ABCD with A on the left, C on the right, D above, and B below. The diagonal AC is drawn horizontally through the rhombus, and point P lies on this diagonal. Point E lies on side AB, with segment PE drawn perpendicular to AB and a right-angle marker at E. Point F lies on side AD, with segment PF perpendicular to AD and a right-angle marker at F. Reasoning: Consider triangle AEP in the figure. AE lies along side AB, AP lies along diagonal AC, and PE is perpendicular to AB, so triangle AEP is right-angled at E. In a rhombus, the diagonal AC bisects angle BAD. Since angle BAD = 60°, angle EAP, which is the angle between AB and AC, is 30°. In right triangle AEP, side PE is opposite the 30° angle, and PE = 1. Therefore the hypotenuse AP = 2PE = 2. Then by the Pythagorean theorem, AE = sqrt(AP^2 - PE^2) = sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3).
